note: Two questions a reader of the public site would ask, left open with options from the site's own words: the owner rules them.

data.question: Which number says sharingu is working for an organization (the aim's measure)?
data.why: A reader of the site finds four kinds of measure (usage, cost, decisions, outcomes) and the rule that each needs a source, unit, time window and status, but no single number the product itself is judged by. The aim is filed without a measure until the owner rules.

options.what: Progress against a goal, supported by evidence and a meaningful baseline (the site's Outcomes measure)
options.tradeoff: Closest to the mission; needs a baseline and attribution before it means anything, which the site says are not established yet.

options.what: Decisions moved forward: human rulings recorded with their reasons and the next contribution they make possible (the site's Decisions measure)
options.tradeoff: Countable from the record from day one; a recorded decision does not by itself prove progress.

options.what: Attributed usage and cost per contribution, with a named budget owner (the site's Usage and Cost measures)
options.tradeoff: Matches the cost-to-outcome claim; unreported usage stays unknown, and the site says live cross-provider metering is not established.

source.label: the home page: what went in, what moved forward

data.question: Which AI clients will the private beta name as supported?
data.why: The site names ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini CLI as examples of tools with MCP support, and says the links are not a completed sharingu integration test; the supported client is confirmed per organization during onboarding. A reader cannot tell which clients work today.

options.what: Name each client on the site once a sharingu integration test passes for it
options.tradeoff: A public list a reader can trust; each name waits for its own test.

options.what: Keep the site's wording: any client with MCP support, confirmed per organization at onboarding
options.tradeoff: No new claim to prove; a reader still has to ask before trying.
